questions.question:
The correct feature of double-helical structure of DNA as given by Watson and Crick is: 
1. Right-handed helix, pitch is \(3.4~ \text {nm}\)
2. Left-handed helix, pitch is \(3.8~ \text {nm}\)
3. Right-handed helix, pitch is \(3.8~ \text {nm}\)

questions.explanation:
The salient features of double-helical structure of DNA given by Watson and Crick are: 1. It is made of two polynucleotide chains. 2. The two chains have anti-parallel polarity. 3. The bases in two strands are paired through hydrogen bond (H-bonds). Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine. Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds. As a result, uniform distance between the two strands of the helix is formed. 4. The two chains are coiled in a right-handed fashion. The pitch of the helix is\(3.4~ \text {nm}\). There are roughly 10 bp in each turn. The distance between a bp in a helix is approximately equal to\(0.34~ \text {nm}\). 5. The plane of one base pair stacks over the other in double helix. This in addition to H-bonds accounts for the stability of the helical structure.

questions.question:
Each tRNA is charged with a specific amino acid by:
1. aminoacyl tRNA synthetase
2. polynucleotide phosphorylase
3. peptidyl transferase
4. topoisomerase
questions.explanation:
Aminoacyl tRNA synthetase is an enzyme that catalyzes the attachment of a specific amino acid to its corresponding tRNA molecule. This process is known as "charging" the tRNA. Each aminoacyl tRNA synthetase is specific for a particular amino acid and recognizes the appropriate tRNA molecule through its anticodon sequence. This ensures that the correct amino acid is attached to the appropriate tRNA molecule, which is essential for accurate protein synthesis. Polynucleotide phosphorylase is an enzyme that can synthesize RNA by polymerizing nucleotides together in the absence of a template. Peptidyl transferase is an enzyme found in the ribosome that catalyzes the formation of peptide bonds between amino acids during translation. Topoisomerase is an enzyme that can modify the supercoiling of DNA by cutting and rejoining the strands.

Termination occurs when a release factor binds to the stop codon and releases the complete polypeptide.

questions.question:
All living organisms - past, present and future are linked to each other. All organisms have arisen from a single distant ancestor. The strongest evidence for this will be:
1.All organisms have a triplet genetic code
2.DNA is the genetic material of almost all living organisms
3.The genetic code is degenerate but non-ambiguous
4.The amino acids specified by particular triplets are almost always identical between any two organisms.
questions.explanation:
* The universality of the genetic code provides the strongest evidence that all living organisms have evolved from a common ancestor. * This means that a given codon specifies the same amino acid in almost all organisms — from bacteria to humans. * For example, the codon AUG codes for methionine in nearly every organism. * Hence, the fact that the amino acids specified by particular triplets are identical across species is the strongest molecular evidence for common ancestry. Option 3- * This statement is true, but it only describes a property of the genetic code — that multiple codons can code for the same amino acid (degeneracy), yet each codon specifies only one amino acid (non-ambiguity). * However, this does not directly prove that all organisms share a common ancestor; it only explains how the code functions within organisms. * Option 4- * This expresses the universality of the genetic code — that the same codon codes for the same amino acid in nearly all living organisms. * This universality provides strong evidence for common ancestry among all living beings. questions.question:
If E. coli were allowed to grow in the culture medium for 80 minutes by Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl in their experiments, the proportion of light and hybrid density DNA molecule would have been: 
1. 87.5% of light density DNA and 12.5% of hybrid density DNA. 
2. 75.0% of light density DNA and 25% of hybrid density DNA. 
3. 50% of light density DNA and 50% of hybrid density DNA.
4. 12.5% of light density DNA and 87.5% of hybrid density DNA.
questions.explanation:
An E.coil divides in every 20 minutes therefore, after 80 minutes it will be four generations. In the first generation, all the strands will be hybrid as the heavy isotope will be incorporated in the newly synthesised strand of DNA. i.e., the two DNA will be intermediate nature. In the second generation, half (50%) will be hybrid and half (50%) will light. In the third generation the 1/4 will be hybrid and 3/4 will be light i.e., 25% will be hybrid and 75% will be light. Finally, in the fourth the above four generation, 12.5% will be hybrid and 87.5% will be light strand.
